question_record.context: A security incident involving a successful logon using overpass-the-hash with potentially stolen credentials occurred on host `vnevado-win10b` using the account of SID S-1-5-21-1540151660-3530000288-105586595-1517. As part of following the activity, suspicious access to the LSASS service was detected, an indication that attackers might have been trying to decrypt user passwords from memory. Later, a known credential theft tool execution was detected indicating an attempt to dump user credentials.
question_record.question: Can you identify the process ID and command line of the malicious credential theft tool that was executed?
solution: An attacker used the process `lsass.exe` to perform an overpass-the-hash attack.
A suspicious access was detected to the LSASS service with SID `S-5-7-21-1843151660-3234030288-105586167-1422`.

A malicious credential theft tool `mimikatz.exe` was executed with Process ID `4748` at `2024-06-27t14:33:38.0249949z` with the command line `mimikatz.exe lsadump::dcsync /domain:vnevado.alpineskihouse.co /user:xfbzkp exit`.

52.name: Successful logon using overpass-the-hash with potentially stolen credentials
52.description: An attacker accessed a resource with credentials that might have been obtained using an overpass-the-hash attack. An overpass-the-hash attack typically involves obtaining a password hash from memory and then using the hash to obtain a Kerberos ticket. The ticket is then used to authenticate to network resources.

102.name: Suspicious access to LSASS service
102.description: In order to obtain clear-text password, attackers must decrypt the user's password from the LSASS service's memory. Multiple public tools as well as custom ones could be used to perform this operation. Once obtained, these credentials are often used in lateral movement activities to infiltrate other machines and servers in the network.

26.name: Malicious credential theft tool execution detected
26.description:
A known credential theft tool execution command line was detected.
Either the process itself or its command line indicated an intent to dump users' credentials, keys, plain-text passwords and more.
